title: Music Trivia Quiz: Legendary Artists, Genres, Albums & Music History
description: Test your music knowledge with questions about legendary artists, iconic albums, genre origins, Grammy awards, and fascinating music history facts.

questions.text: Which album by Michael Jackson became the best-selling album of all time, with estimated sales exceeding 70 million copies worldwide?
questions.explanation: Thriller (1982) is certified as the best-selling album ever with over 70 million copies sold. It produced seven singles including 'Billie Jean', 'Beat It', and the title track, and won a record-breaking eight Grammy Awards at the 1984 ceremony.

questions.text: Jazz music originated in the early 20th century primarily in which American city?
questions.explanation: Jazz emerged in New Orleans, Louisiana in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, blending African American musical traditions including blues, ragtime, and spirituals with European harmonies. The city's diverse cultural melting pot provided the perfect environment for this new genre.

questions.text: Which artist has won the most Grammy Awards in history?
questions.explanation: Beyoncé holds the record for the most Grammy Awards ever won by any artist with 32 wins (as of 2024). She surpassed the previous record of 31 held by conductor Georg Solti, spanning categories across pop, R&B, music video, and more.

questions.text: In music theory, what is the term for a sequence of notes that sounds complete and forms the basis of a melody?
questions.explanation: A scale is an ordered sequence of notes spanning an octave that provides the tonal foundation for melodies and harmonies. The most common are the major scale (happy/bright sound) and minor scale (sad/dark sound), each with a specific pattern of whole and half steps.

questions.text: The Beatles officially broke up in 1970. In which city did all four members — John, Paul, George, and Ringo — originally meet and form the band?
questions.explanation: The Beatles were formed in Liverpool, England in 1960. John Lennon and Paul McCartney met at a church fete in 1957, later recruiting George Harrison and eventually Ringo Starr. Liverpool's Cavern Club became legendary as their early performance venue.

questions.text: Which song holds the record for the most weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 chart?
questions.explanation: Lil Nas X's 'Old Town Road' (featuring Billy Ray Cyrus) spent 19 weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2019, breaking the previous record of 16 weeks held by both 'One Sweet Day' by Mariah Carey & Boyz II Men and 'Despacito' by Luis Fonsi & Daddy Yankee (remix ft. Justin Bieber).

answers.text: Shape of You by Ed Sheeran
Despacito by Luis Fonsi ft. Daddy Yankee
Old Town Road by Lil Nas X ft. Billy Ray Cyrus

questions.text: Woodstock, one of the most iconic music festivals in history, took place in 1969. In which U.S. state was it held?
questions.explanation: Woodstock was held on a dairy farm in Bethel, New York (not in the town of Woodstock, despite its name). The three-day festival attracted an estimated 400,000 attendees and featured performances by Jimi Hendrix, Janis Joplin, The Who, and many other legendary artists.

questions.text: The piano has 88 keys in its standard modern form. How many of those keys are white?
questions.explanation: A standard 88-key piano has 52 white keys and 36 black keys. The white keys represent the natural notes (A through G), while the black keys represent sharps and flats. This 7+5 pattern repeats across just over seven octaves.

questions.text: Which genre originated in the Bronx, New York in the 1970s, combining DJing, MCing, breakdancing, and graffiti art?
questions.explanation: Hip-hop culture emerged in the South Bronx in the early 1970s, pioneered by DJs like Kool Herc, Afrika Bambaataa, and Grandmaster Flash. It encompassed four elements: DJing, MCing (rapping), breakdancing (b-boying), and graffiti art, growing into one of the world's dominant cultural movements.

questions.text: The songwriting duo of Lennon-McCartney is one of music's most celebrated partnerships. Under what agreement were most of their songs credited?
questions.explanation: Lennon and McCartney agreed early on to credit all their songs as 'Lennon-McCartney' regardless of who primarily wrote a particular song. This meant songs largely written by one (like McCartney's 'Yesterday' or Lennon's 'Strawberry Fields Forever') still carried the joint credit.

answers.text: Each song was credited to its primary writer individually
All songs were credited jointly as 'Lennon-McCartney' regardless of individual contribution
Songs were credited to 'The Beatles' as a group with no individual names
Credits alternated between albums — one album Lennon, next album McCartney
